judged_text: createEvent selects the target calendar solely via `find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`, which can never match when the destination has no credentialId (the EventManager else-branch passes credentials whose ids differ from the null destination.credentialId), so selectedCalendar is undefined and the event is inserted into 'primary'. For DestinationCalendar rows with null credentialId, events land on the user's primary calendar instead of the chosen destination calendar (pre-diff code inserted into destinationCalendar.externalId), while the stored reference still points at the destination's externalId, so later updates/deletes target a calendar that never held the event.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent` now selects `calendarId` via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and falls back to `"primary"` when not found. In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` `createAllCalendarEvents`, the else-branch for destinations without `destination.credentialId` calls `createEvent(c, event)` (no externalId passed), so `CalendarManager.createEvent` invokes `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` with only the credential id. If the destination calendar objects have `credentialId` null/undefined (the scenario described), the `find(...credentialId === credentialId)` cannot match, making `selectedCalendar` undefined and causing insertion into `primary` (`calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`). This is a concrete behavioral change from the pre-diff behavior (which used `destinationCalendar.externalId` directly) and can route events to the wrong calendar for destination calendars lacking a credentialId.
